query: Refactor BlogEditor: its View now takes 34 props across a server-provided stats block, a header with save/edit actions, and a form with per-keystroke fields. The stats do not depend on the draft, but editing a field re-renders the stats block. A teammate suggests putting shared state in one Context to keep the change small.
baseline_failure: Agent keeps growing one controller/View prop list, or introduces one big Context whose value is rebuilt every render so every sub-section re-renders on each keystroke.
expected_behavior: Moves per-keystroke form state into the form subtree or a focused colocated provider
Uses props while they remain clear and splits Context only by distinct consumer sets or update frequencies
A Stats block does not subscribe to form state and does not re-render on form input
Explains the ownership or measured-render reason for any provider or memoization boundary
anti_expectation: Does NOT apply the compound-provider split to a small component that is clear with a direct named Hook call
Does NOT bundle fetched data, mutation state, and form values into one Context
Does NOT create a fixed Data/Mutations/FormState/FormActions provider set just to match a template
evaluation_note: The old four-provider recipe had RED-to-GREEN evidence, but that query and expected implementation were retired. A 2026-07-29 rerun did not reproduce the corrected ownership failure on gpt-5.6-luna, so this scenario is a hypothesis rather than current evidence.
